review.standard: Vitest rules: Errors & Callback Assertions — wrap the call so the matcher catches the throw (expect(() => fn()).toThrow); match the repo's style (test/cart.test.js:10 uses expect(() => …).toThrow(RangeError))
review.summary: The unknown-coupon tests capture the error with a hand-written try/catch into a `let` instead of asserting through `expect(() => …).toThrow(UnknownCouponError)` / `.toThrow('"SAVE99"')`, unlike the repo's existing tests.
review.failureScenario: Nothing passes wrongly, because the assertions sit outside the catch: if couponDiscount('SAVE99', 2000) stopped throwing, `error` would be undefined and toBeInstanceOf would fail. But the failure would read 'expected undefined to be an instance of UnknownCouponError' rather than the matcher's 'function did not throw', and the try/catch is the anti-pattern the standards name. The same pattern is at test/pricing.test.js:52-60 (TC10). Both could be `expect(() => …).toThrow(UnknownCouponError)` followed by `expect(() => …).toThrow('"NOPE"')`.
